title: How We Got Here
summary: An earlier public introduction: the name, the promise, and a reason to keep the door open for someone else.
paragraphs: This is an introduction to GhostHeart, not an excerpt from the book. The deeper life story will unfold through selected pages. Begin here with the purpose behind it.

GhostHeart is one lived story told through music, film, words, and visual storytelling. But the music is not the whole story. It opens a door into the experiences, questions, relationships, and choices behind it.
The heart survived. Then it chose a purpose.

Survival matters. So does what a person chooses to carry forward. GhostHeart turns toward people who have been reduced to a label, judged from a distance, or written off before their story was heard. Seeing their humanity does not mean looking away from the truth or excusing harm. It means refusing to let one word tell the whole story.

That is where the name meets the promise. This Is GhostHeart introduces the heart behind the work. GhostHeart’s Oath gives that heart a direction: protect the light in others. The films below belong together, but you can begin with either one.

Love belongs here too. The Woman Behind the Scenes is the relationship story within this larger world—the person who saw the heart beneath the scars and never asked it to hide. It has its own place, alongside the music and the life behind it.

You do not have to share this past to find something in these words. Stay with a song. Carry a line that means something to you. Find support when you need more than a story can offer. No one has to disclose their own pain to belong here.

The written book carries a deeper life story. This public beginning stops before those private pages. Sunday readings will connect selected pages to the work unfolding around them; reading details will be announced when they are confirmed.
For now, meet the name. Hear the promise. Then choose what you want to carry forward.

title: This is GhostHeart.
summary: A heart that survived, and a question about what comes next.
paragraphs: This Is GhostHeart begins with a heart that survived and a question about what comes next. The song opens a larger story told through music, film, words and pictures.
What can a person carry forward from survival? And how might that become something another person can recognize themselves in?

title: GhostHeart’s Oath
summary: What might protecting the light in others look like in an ordinary moment?
paragraphs: GhostHeart’s Oath turns from the name to the promise behind it: protecting the light in others.
What might that promise look like in an ordinary moment? What survived can become a reason to help someone else rise.

title: You’re Not God
summary: A question about belief, judgement and the difference between care and control.
paragraphs: Where does belief end and control begin?
You’re Not God explores that question through songs about judgement, shame and people who claim the right to speak for heaven. Its focus is what happens when faith is used to hurt or exclude someone.
That Ain’t Holy and Hey Preacher Man ask what happens when compassion becomes control and religion is used to excuse cruelty.
Belief can matter deeply to a person. That does not give someone else the right to decide whose love counts or whose life has value.
The album holds those ideas together: room for faith, and a boundary against cruelty carried out in its name.

title: Cruel — Something Needs to Change
summary: What happens after the video ends?
paragraphs: What happens after the video ends?
That’s the question I want Cruel to leave with us. The crowd moves on, but the person we watched still has to live with what happened.
It’s easy to see one reaction and think we understand someone. What might we be missing? What has made it hard for that person to trust kindness?

One conversation won’t undo years of hurt. Sometimes someone needs more help than we can offer. But a patient response can still matter: time to finish a sentence, a question asked without judgement, or kindness that doesn’t depend on hearing their whole story.
If you’re the person who is hurting, you don’t owe anyone your whole story to deserve kindness.
For me, the song returns to those small choices. I’m interested in care that reaches someone in an ordinary moment, even when we don’t have all the answers.
When someone is already hurting, what could we offer that makes the next moment a little less lonely?
